input.summary: src/click/shell_completion.py implements Click's shell completion. shell_complete() parses an instruction such as "bash_source" or "zsh_complete" from an env var. It looks up a ShellComplete subclass in the `_available_shells` registry. It then either prints the shell script (`source`) or the formatted completions (`complete`). Completion resolves a Context chain from the already-typed args (`_resolve_context`), picks the object that completes the incomplete word (`_resolve_incomplete`), and calls that object's `shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`. That call returns a list of CompletionItem. Each shell subclass supplies a script template (`source_template`), env-var parsing (`get_completion_args`) and an output wire format (`format_completion`). Wire formats: bash and fish use "type,value" lines (fish adds a tab and help), while zsh and powershell use 3-line "type\nvalue\nhelp" records with "_" as the no-help sentinel. Custom shells can be registered with add_completion_class.

interfaces.name: shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Entry point (line 19). Splits `instruction` with partition('_') into shell and instruction. Looks up the class with get_completion_class, instantiates it as comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var), and returns 0 or 1. 'source' echoes comp.source() as encoded bytes with nl=False. 'complete' echoes comp.complete() as encoded bytes, with a trailing newline. Bytes are written so Windows does not turn LF into CRLF.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns 1
Unknown instruction returns 1
Instruction without '_' gives shell=whole string and instruction='' so it returns 1 (or 1 for unknown shell)
The shell name is the part before the first underscore, so registered names containing '_' can never match

interfaces.name: CompletionItem
interfaces.behavior: Generic class with __slots__ value, type, help, _info (line 67). Defaults: type='plain', help=None. Extra **kwargs are kept in _info and read as attributes through __getattr__.
edge_cases: Unknown attribute returns None instead of raising AttributeError
type values the built-in shell scripts handle: plain, dir, file; any other type is ignored by the bash, fish and powershell scripts

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Returns self._info.get(name), so missing metadata is None (line 100).
edge_cases: Only called for attributes not found normally

interfaces.name: ShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: Base class (line 277, versionadded 8.0). Holds cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var. Subclasses must set the class vars `name` and `source_template`.
edge_cases: get_completion_args and format_completion are abstract and raise NotImplementedError in the base class
The base class can be used directly to call get_completions (tests do this)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Stores cli, ctx_args (a mutable mapping), prog_name and complete_var (line 306).
edge_cases: ctx_args is later mutated by _resolve_context, which sets resilient_parsing=True

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.func_name
interfaces.behavior: Property (line 318). Replaces '-' with '_' in prog_name, strips non-word ASCII characters with re.sub(r'\W*', '', flags=re.ASCII), and returns f'_{safe}_completion'.
edge_cases: A prog_name with only symbols gives '__completion'

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
interfaces.behavior: Returns the dict used to format source_template (line 326), with keys complete_func (func_name), complete_var and prog_name.
edge_cases: Subclasses can add keys, though the _SourceVarsDict TypedDict only declares three

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Returns source_template % source_vars() (line 338).
edge_cases: A literal '%' in a custom template must be written as '%%', otherwise the formatting fails
The result is encoded and written without a trailing newline by shell_complete

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 346). Must return (args, incomplete) read from env vars.

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
interfaces.behavior: Line 353. Calls _resolve_context, then _resolve_incomplete, then obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete). Returns a list of CompletionItem.
edge_cases: Empty incomplete is allowed
args may be mutated by _resolve_incomplete (an '--opt=value' split appends the option name)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 367). Turns one CompletionItem into the shell wire string.

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.complete
interfaces.behavior: Line 375. Calls get_completion_args, then get_completions, then format_completion on each item. Joins the results with '\n'.
edge_cases: No completions gives an empty string; shell_complete's echo then still adds a newline
The result has no trailing newline of its own, since echo adds one

interfaces.name: BashComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='bash', template _SOURCE_BASH (line 388). The script runs `env COMP_WORDS=... COMP_CWORD=... VAR=bash_complete $1`, then handles types: dir sets compopt -o dirnames, file sets compopt -o default, plain appends to COMPREPLY. The script registers with `complete -o nosort`, which needs Bash >= 4.4.
edge_cases: The bash script ignores item.help

interfaces.name: BashComplete._check_version
interfaces.behavior: Static method (line 394). Finds bash with shutil.which and runs `bash --norc -c 'echo ${BASH_VERSION}'`. Prints a translated warning to stderr if the version is below 4.4, or if bash is not found or the version can't be parsed.
edge_cases: Never aborts; it only warns on stderr
The version comparison is done on strings, so '10' < '4' is True (a bug for major versions >= 10)
Tests monkeypatch it

interfaces.name: BashComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Calls _check_version(), then super().source() (line 427).
edge_cases: Runs a subprocess on every source call

interfaces.name: BashComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Line 431. Splits env COMP_WORDS with split_arg_string. cword=int(env COMP_CWORD). args=cwords[1:cword]. incomplete=cwords[cword], or '' on IndexError.
edge_cases: A missing env var raises KeyError
A non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError

interfaces.name: BashComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Returns f'{type},{value}' (line 443). The help text is dropped.
edge_cases: A value containing a comma or newline is not escaped; the script does `IFS=',' read type value`, which keeps the rest of the line in value

interfaces.name: ZshComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='zsh', template _SOURCE_ZSH (line 447). The script uses _describe for items with help and compadd for items without. It is frozen for backwards compatibility, so changes go into format_completion.

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 465. help_ = item.help or '_'. Escapes ':' as '\:' in the value only when help is present (not '_'). Returns 'type\nvalue\nhelp'.
edge_cases: A real help text of '_' is treated as no help
A multi-line help is not sanitized

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same as BashComplete: COMP_WORDS and COMP_CWORD, args=cwords[1:cword] (line 453).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError
Non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError

interfaces.name: FishComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='fish', template _SOURCE_FISH (line 479). get_completion_args (line 485) reads COMP_WORDS (the whole command line) and COMP_CWORD (the current token, not an index). The incomplete word is split_arg_string(COMP_CWORD)[0] when non-empty. args=cwords[1:], and the last element is popped if it equals incomplete.
edge_cases: COMP_CWORD='' gives an empty incomplete
A quoted partial word is unquoted
A missing env var raises KeyError

interfaces.name: FishComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 499. With help: 'type,value\thelp', where newlines in the help become literal backslash-n and tabs become spaces. Without help: 'type,value'.
edge_cases: An empty help string is treated as no help

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='powershell', template _SOURCE_POWERSHELL (line 516, versionadded 8.5.0). The template uses Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native and parses the output 3 lines at a time. Types: plain gives a CompletionResult with a tooltip; dir and file use Get-ChildItem with a prefix glob.
edge_cases: The prefix for dir/file is wordToComplete+'*'

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 537. Same 3-line format as zsh. Help has \r and \n replaced by spaces ('_' if no help). The value is not escaped.
edge_cases: CRLF becomes two spaces
A value containing a newline would break the framing

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same logic as Bash and Zsh (line 525).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError

interfaces.name: add_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Registers cls in the module-level `_available_shells` under name or cls.name and returns cls, so it works as a decorator (line 560).
edge_cases: Overwrites an existing entry silently
No validation of the name

gaps.description: Value escaping is inconsistent. Bash and PowerShell values containing commas or newlines are not escaped, and zsh help is not newline-sanitized.

gaps.description: No auto-detection of the shell, and no built-in install command that writes the script to the shell's rc or completions directory.

gaps.description: Env var parsing failures (KeyError or ValueError) are not handled gracefully in get_completion_args.

limitations: The shell is parsed with instruction.partition('_'), so registered shell names cannot contain underscores.
The zsh script is frozen for backwards compatibility, so only format_completion can change zsh behavior.
Bash completion requires Bash >= 4.4 (the nosort option). The check only warns on stderr, and the string comparison of versions is buggy for majors >= 10.
The source output has no trailing newline (nl=False). The complete output is utf-8 encoded bytes.
Completion runs with resilient_parsing=True and does not invoke callbacks or prompts. _resolve_context mutates the passed ctx_args.
Options are recognized through ctx._opt_prefixes, a private attribute.
The PowerShell script treats the dir and file types with a Get-ChildItem glob on the prefix and ignores the item's value.
Only the plain, dir and file item types are understood by the built-in scripts.

input.summary: src/click/termui.py holds Click's interactive and terminal helpers. It has prompt/confirm built on a swappable `visible_prompt_func` (input) and `hidden_prompt_func` (getpass). It also has ANSI style/unstyle/secho, and thin lazy wrappers over `_termui_impl` (progressbar, edit, launch, getchar, raw_terminal, pager). It also has clear and pause. Prompts go through `_readline_prompt`, which passes the full prompt text to the input function so readline works. It strips ANSI itself when the stream doesn't support color.

interfaces.name: prompt
interfaces.behavior: Builds the prompt via _build_prompt (text, then ' (choices)' if type is a Choice and show_choices, then ' [default]' if show_default, then prompt_suffix default ': '). If value_proc is None it uses convert_type(type, default). Loops reading input via hidden_prompt_func if hide_input, else visible_prompt_func. Empty input returns the default if default is not None, otherwise it re-prompts forever. The default is cast and passed through value_proc like typed input. A UsageError from value_proc prints 'Error: <message>' (via echo, to stderr if err) and re-prompts. With hide_input the message is masked via _mask_hidden_input. confirmation_prompt (True gives 'Repeat for confirmation', or a custom string) asks a second time. A mismatch prints 'Error: The two entered values do not match.' and restarts. If both are empty, confirmation is accepted.
edge_cases: show_default as str shows ' [(str)]' instead of the value
default of None with empty input re-prompts
File defaults are shown by name via _format_default
KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError become Abort; with hide_input a newline is echoed first
empty confirmation re-asks unless the first value was also empty

interfaces.name: confirm
interfaces.behavior: Yes/no prompt. The suffix is '[Y/n]', '[y/N]' or '[y/n]' depending on default (True, False, None), shown only if show_default. Input is lowercased and stripped. y/yes gives True, n/no gives False, and empty returns default when it is not None. Anything else echoes 'Error: invalid input' and re-asks. If abort=True a negative answer raises Abort.
edge_cases: default=None repeats until a valid answer
EOF/KeyboardInterrupt raise Abort

interfaces.name: hidden_prompt_func
interfaces.behavior: Imports getpass lazily and returns getpass.getpass(prompt). It is a module-level hook that tests and doc tools monkeypatch.

interfaces.name: get_pager_file
interfaces.behavior: Resolves color with resolve_color_default, then delegates to _termui_impl.get_pager_file(color=...). It returns a context manager yielding a writable text file for the pager (new in 8.4.0).
edge_cases: color=None means autodetect

interfaces.name: echo_via_pager
interfaces.behavior: Accepts a str, an iterable, or a generator function (called with no args). A str becomes a one-item list. Each element is coerced to str. Writes via get_pager_file, flushing after each write, and appends a final '\n' (chained as an iterable of characters).
edge_cases: non-str elements are str()'d
only generator functions, not other callables, are called

interfaces.name: progressbar
interfaces.behavior: Resolves color, then builds and returns _termui_impl.ProgressBar with all args forwarded. It is used as a context manager and iterable. Defaults: show_eta=True, fill '#', empty '-', template '%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s', info_sep two spaces, width 36 (0 means full terminal width), update_min_steps=1. The overloads require length when there is no iterable. If the file is not a TTY only the label is printed, and hidden=True suppresses even that.
edge_cases: item_show_func may receive None
show_percent defaults to True only if the length is known

interfaces.name: clear
interfaces.behavior: If stdout is a TTY, echoes '\033[2J\033[1;1H' with nl=False. Otherwise it does nothing.
edge_cases: no-op when not a TTY

interfaces.name: style
interfaces.behavior: Converts non-str text with str(). Builds ANSI codes in this order: fg, bg (offset 10), bold, dim, underline, overline, italic, blink, reverse, strikethrough. Each flag None is skipped, True turns it on, False emits the off code (22, 24, 55, 23, 25, 27, 29). Appends the text, then '\033[0m' if reset=True. Colors can be a name, an int 0-255 (8-bit), or an RGB tuple/list.
edge_cases: bold=False and dim=False both emit 22
reset=False allows composing styles
bool colors are rejected

interfaces.name: unstyle
interfaces.behavior: Returns strip_ansi(text) with ANSI codes removed.

interfaces.name: secho
interfaces.behavior: Calls style(message, **styles) unless message is None or bytes/bytearray, then echo(message, file, nl, err, color). Bytes skip styling. Style kwargs are forwarded to style, so a bad kwarg raises TypeError and a bad color raises ValueError.
edge_cases: None message goes to echo unstyled (prints a blank line)
unknown style kwarg raises TypeError from style()

interfaces.name: edit
interfaces.behavior: Builds _termui_impl.Editor(editor, env, require_save, extension). With filename=None it returns ed.edit(text). Otherwise a str or PathLike is wrapped in a tuple and ed.edit_files is called, returning None. The overloads give require_save default False for bytes and True for str. Per the docstring, a UsageError is raised if the editor cannot be opened (raised inside Editor, not read here).
edge_cases: returns None if unchanged and require_save
filename makes text, require_save and extension irrelevant

interfaces.name: launch
interfaces.behavior: Delegates to _termui_impl.open_url(url, wait, locate) and returns the exit code (0 usually means success). locate=True opens a file manager at the file.
edge_cases: xdg-open does not block even with wait=True

interfaces.name: getchar
interfaces.behavior: Lazily imports and caches _termui_impl.getchar in the module global _getchar, then calls it with echo (default False). Tests set click.termui._getchar to override it.
edge_cases: may return more than one character
reads from the terminal even if stdin is piped

interfaces.name: raw_terminal
interfaces.behavior: Returns the context manager from _termui_impl.raw_terminal() (yields an int). It has no docstring.

interfaces.name: pause
interfaces.behavior: Returns immediately unless both stdin and stdout are TTYs. Default info is 'Press any key to continue...'. Echoes the info with nl=False, calls getchar(), and swallows KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError. In a finally block it echoes a newline if info is truthy. info='' prints nothing.
edge_cases: no-op when not interactive
empty info means no message and no newline

interfaces.name: _readline_prompt
interfaces.behavior: Private helper that picks stderr or stdout. It strips ANSI from the text if _compat.should_strip_ansi(stream, resolve_color_default()) is true; this is looked up on the module so CliRunner's patch applies. It calls func(text), wrapped in redirect_stdout(sys.stderr) when err=True.

interfaces.name: _build_prompt
interfaces.behavior: Private helper that assembles the prompt string from text, choices, a default preview and the suffix. It is also used by confirm with a 'y/n' style pseudo-default.

interfaces.name: _mask_hidden_input
interfaces.behavior: Replaces repr(value) and the raw value (word-boundary regex, skipped when value is empty) in an error message with "'***'" so hidden input doesn't leak.
edge_cases: empty value skips the raw pass

interfaces.name: _interpret_color
interfaces.behavior: Private helper that maps a color name, int 0-255 or 3-int tuple/list to an SGR parameter string. The offset (10 for bg) is added to named colors and applied to 38 for 8-bit and RGB colors.
edge_cases: bools rejected
out-of-range ints and bad tuples raise ValueError

input.error_conventions: Abort is raised for user interrupt/EOF, or for a declined confirm(abort=True). UsageError from type conversion is caught inside prompt and shown as the message 'Error: <message>' (gettext-wrapped), followed by a re-prompt. confirm prints 'Error: invalid input'. The confirmation mismatch message is 'Error: The two entered values do not match.' ValueError('Unknown color {colour!r}') is raised for bad colors. UsageError for editor failures comes from _termui_impl, not this file. Errors are written with echo(err=err).

input.summary: src/click/exceptions.py defines Click's exception hierarchy. ClickException (exit_code 1) is the base for user-facing errors. It has format_message() and show(). UsageError (exit_code 2) prints usage and a help hint. Its subclasses are BadParameter, MissingParameter, NoSuchOption, NoSuchCommand, BadOptionUsage, BadArgumentUsage and NoArgsIsHelpError. FileError is a direct ClickException subclass. Abort and Exit are NOT ClickExceptions: they derive from RuntimeError and are control-flow signals. Command.main in core.py (about lines 1571-1612) catches them. In standalone mode it calls e.show and sys.exit(e.exit_code). In non-standalone mode it re-raises ClickException and Abort, and returns Exit.exit_code.

interfaces.name: ClickException
interfaces.behavior: Base class (line 35). __init__(message) calls Exception.__init__, caches show_color = resolve_color_default() at construction (the context is gone by the time show runs), and stores message. Class attribute exit_code = 1. format_message() returns self.message. __str__ returns self.message. show(file=None) writes 'Error: {message}' via echo to file, or to get_text_stderr() if file is None, using the cached show_color.
edge_cases: file=None means stderr
message is not validated, so a non-str message would break __str__

interfaces.name: ClickException.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.message. Subclasses override it to decorate the message. show() uses it.

interfaces.name: ClickException.show
interfaces.behavior: Prints 'Error: <format_message()>' to the given file or to stderr. Color comes from the value cached at construction.
edge_cases: file None -> stderr

interfaces.name: UsageError
interfaces.behavior: Line 68. exit_code = 2. __init__(message, ctx=None) stores ctx and sets cmd = ctx.command if ctx else None. show() prints, in order: ctx.get_usage(), then a "Try '<command_path> <longest help option name>' for help." line only if the command has a help option, then 'Error: <message>'. Color comes from ctx.color. Without a ctx it prints only the Error line, with color=None.
edge_cases: ctx None -> no usage and no hint
help option disabled (get_help_option returns None) -> no hint
longest help name is chosen with max(key=len)

interfaces.name: UsageError.show
interfaces.behavior: Prints usage, the optional help hint, then 'Error: ...' to file or stderr. Uses ctx.color, not the cached show_color.
edge_cases: ctx None
no help option

interfaces.name: BadParameter
interfaces.behavior: Line 114. __init__(message, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None). format_message() uses param_hint if it is not None. Otherwise it uses param.get_error_hint(ctx). If neither is set it returns 'Invalid value: {message}'. Otherwise it returns 'Invalid value for {hint}: {message}'. A sequence hint is joined with ' / ' with each item repr-quoted (_join_param_hints). A str hint is used as-is.
edge_cases: both param and param_hint -> param_hint wins
neither set -> 'Invalid value: msg'
empty-list hint -> empty string

interfaces.name: BadParameter.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Builds 'Invalid value for X: msg', or 'Invalid value: msg' when there is no hint and no param.
edge_cases: see BadParameter

interfaces.name: MissingParameter
interfaces.behavior: Line 159. __init__(message=None, ctx=None, param=None, param_hint=None, param_type=None). A None message becomes ''. format_message builds 'Missing {argument|option|parameter|<custom>} {hint}.{ msg}'. param_type falls back to param.param_type_name. If param is set, param.type.get_missing_message(param, ctx) is appended to the message: joined with '. ' if the message is non-empty, used alone otherwise. An unknown param_type is formatted as 'Missing {param_type}'. __str__ returns the message, or 'Missing parameter: {param.name}' if the message is empty.
edge_cases: empty message -> __str__ uses the param name, which is None if there is no param
param_type None and no param -> 'Missing None'
hint omitted -> no hint text

interfaces.name: MissingParameter.format_message
interfaces.behavior: See MissingParameter. Translates the known param types and appends the type's missing message (for example a Choice lists its choices).
edge_cases: unknown param_type

interfaces.name: MissingParameter.__str__
interfaces.behavior: Returns self.message, or a 'Missing parameter: name' fallback when the message is empty.
edge_cases: param None -> 'Missing parameter: None'

interfaces.name: NoSuchOption
interfaces.behavior: Line 232. __init__(option_name, message=None, possibilities=None, ctx=None). The default message is "No such option 'x'." Possibilities are filtered with difflib.get_close_matches(option_name, possibilities) (default n=3, cutoff 0.6). format_message appends a sorted 'Did you mean ...?' suggestion (ngettext singular/plural) when matches exist. Stores option_name and possibilities (None when empty).
edge_cases: falsy possibilities -> None
no close match -> empty list, no suggestion

interfaces.name: NoSuchCommand
interfaces.behavior: Line 268, added in 8.4.0. Same pattern as NoSuchOption: command_name, default message "No such command 'x'.", fuzzy possibilities via difflib, and the same format_message suggestion.
edge_cases: same as NoSuchOption

interfaces.name: BadOptionUsage
interfaces.behavior: Line 304. __init__(option_name, message, ctx=None). A UsageError that stores option_name. It is raised when an option is used incorrectly, such as the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: BadArgumentUsage
interfaces.behavior: Line 323. UsageError subclass with no overrides. Raised when an argument is used incorrectly, such as the wrong number of values.

interfaces.name: NoArgsIsHelpError
interfaces.behavior: Line 332. __init__(ctx) calls super().__init__(ctx.get_help(), ctx=ctx), so the message is the full help text. show() echoes format_message() to stderr (err=True) with ctx.color, without the 'Error:' prefix or usage. It inherits exit_code 2.
edge_cases: ctx is required
show ignores a file argument's usage but passes file through to echo; err=True is used when file is None

interfaces.name: FileError
interfaces.behavior: Line 342. __init__(filename, hint=None). A None hint becomes 'unknown error'. ui_filename = format_filename(filename) (surrogate-safe) and the raw filename is stored. format_message returns "Could not open file {ui_filename!r}: {message}". exit_code is inherited as 1.
edge_cases: a surrogate filename renders as the replacement char U+FFFD
hint None -> 'unknown error'

interfaces.name: FileError.format_message
interfaces.behavior: Returns "Could not open file '<ui_filename>': <hint>".
edge_cases: see FileError

interfaces.name: Abort
interfaces.behavior: Line 362. A RuntimeError subclass, not a ClickException, with no custom attributes. In standalone mode, main prints 'Aborted!' (via _echo_aborted) and exits with code 1. In non-standalone mode it re-raises. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError are converted into Abort in non-standalone mode.

interfaces.name: Exit
interfaces.behavior: Line 366. A RuntimeError subclass with __slots__ ('exit_code',). __init__(code=0) sets exit_code. It does not call super().__init__. Context.exit raises it (core.py:831). In non-standalone mode main returns e.exit_code. In standalone mode it calls sys.exit(code).
edge_cases: code is not validated
default 0
no message or args, so str(e) is empty

input.error_conventions: ClickException subclasses are user-facing errors. main() prints them as 'Error: <msg>' and exits with exit_code. exit_code is 1 for ClickException and FileError, and 2 for UsageError and all its subclasses. UsageError, BadParameter, MissingParameter and the NoSuch*/BadOption* classes also print usage and a help hint when a ctx is attached. Abort and Exit are RuntimeError control-flow signals, not ClickExceptions. Message style is a capitalized sentence, usually ending with a period for the NoSuch* and Missing messages. User-visible strings go through gettext (_ and ngettext). Parameter names are quoted with repr, and multiple hints are joined with ' / '. Core also raises UsageError(message, ctx) from Context.fail (core.py:817) and Exit from Context.exit (core.py:831).

extension_points.name: ClickException subclassing (override exit_code / format_message / show)
extension_points.what_could_attach: Custom user-facing errors: subclass ClickException, set exit_code, override format_message or show. Command.main handles them automatically (core.py:1597).

extension_points.name: UsageError.show
extension_points.what_could_attach: Custom usage rendering, such as a different help hint or JSON output.

extension_points.name: Command.main exception dispatch
extension_points.what_could_attach: A new handled exception type, or a global error reporter, added to the except chain.

extension_points.name: _format_possibilities / difflib suggestions
extension_points.what_could_attach: Shared suggestion formatting that other 'did you mean' errors could reuse.

gaps.description: There is no exit-code override on the constructor, so a custom code needs a subclass.
gaps.why_plausible: Exit already takes a code, so an optional exit_code argument is a small step.

gaps.description: There is no structured or machine-readable output, such as to_dict or JSON, for errors.
gaps.why_plausible: Errors already carry param, option_name and possibilities as attributes.

gaps.description: There is no fuzzy-match tuning (n and cutoff are fixed to the difflib defaults) and no suggestions for BadParameter or Choice errors.
gaps.why_plausible: NoSuchOption and NoSuchCommand duplicate the same possibilities logic, which could be factored out and parameterized.

gaps.description: Abort carries no message and Exit carries no message, so there is no custom 'Aborted!' text.
gaps.why_plausible: main prints a fixed 'Aborted!'.

limitations: ClickException.message and show_color are Final, so subclasses cannot reassign them. show_color is captured at construction.
Abort and Exit are not ClickExceptions, so `except ClickException` does not catch them.
Exit.__init__ does not call super().__init__, so args is empty. Exit is slotted, but it inherits __dict__ from RuntimeError.
MissingParameter.__str__ and format_message differ: str gives the raw message or 'Missing parameter: name', while show gives the full formatted text.
NoArgsIsHelpError.show uses err=True, so its output goes to stderr only when file is None.
The only test for this module that I read covers FileError.format_message; other classes have no dedicated tests in tests/test_exceptions.

**Latest Click releases** (from the pallets/click GitHub Releases page; the page doesn't show years)

**8.5.1** (06 Nov, marked Latest): Bug-fix release. Fixes `copy.deepcopy()` and `pickle` on parameters and commands, and prevents unhandled tracebacks from `KeyboardInterrupt` during `Command.main()`. Also adds `Option.get_help_spec()`, a `help` argument on `Parameter`, and several help-text fixes.

**8.5.0** (27 Aug): Feature release. Adds PowerShell shell completion, enables ANSI styles on supported Windows versions (Colorama is no longer used), and adds `Argument(help=...)` with a "Positional arguments" help section. Also adds `custom_version_option`, deprecates `CliRunner.isolated_filesystem` and `get_binary_stream`/`get_text_stream`, and makes `prompt()` generically typed.

**8.4.2** (26 Jun): Bug-fix release. Repairs Fish completion broken in 8.4.0, fixes usage help for optional-argument groups, and makes `echo_via_pager` stream output incrementally. The release notes say "Click 8.4.1 fix release," which appears to be a typo.

**8.4.1** (22 May): Bug-fix release. Restores `get_parameter_source()` during eager callbacks and type conversion, fixes Zsh completion on Windows, and fixes a closed-file error with `echo_via_pager`.

**8.4.0** (17 May): Feature release. Makes `ParamType` a generic base class with narrowed return types, adds `get_pager_file`, adds a `NoSuchCommand` exception with suggestions for misspelled commands, and adds a `capture="fd"` mode to `CliRunner`.

**8.3.3** (22 Apr): Bug-fix release. Replaces `shell=True` with `shlex.split` for pager and editor commands, fixes `default=True` on boolean flags, and patches `pdb.Pdb` in `CliRunner` so debuggers can use the real terminal.

**8.3.2** (03 Apr): Bug-fix release. Fixes `flag_value` handling when `is_flag=False`, hides `Sentinel.UNSET` as `None` in `lookup_default()`, and fixes stream-closing issues in `CliRunner`.

input.summary: src/click/formatting.py holds click's in-memory help rendering. It has module helpers (measure_table, iter_rows, wrap_text, join_options), the HelpFormatter class, and a module global FORCED_WIDTH that CliRunner sets to 80 during invoke. wrap_text delegates to click._textwrap.TextWrapper and is ANSI-aware via term_len. HelpFormatter buffers strings and exposes write_usage, write_heading, write_text, write_dl and the section/indentation context managers. Context.make_formatter (core.py:638) builds it from terminal_width and max_content_width, and Context.formatter_class (core.py:315) is the subclass hook.

interfaces.name: wrap_text
interfaces.behavior: Expands tabs, then wraps with click._textwrap.TextWrapper (replace_whitespace=False). Defaults: width=78, no indents, preserve_paragraphs=False (single-paragraph wrap via wrapper.fill). With preserve_paragraphs=True, lines are grouped into paragraphs split on empty lines. The first line's leading indent (measured with term_len) is kept as an extra indent for the paragraph. A paragraph whose first line is just '\b' is emitted unwrapped via indent_only, with the \b line dropped. Other paragraphs have their lines joined with spaces and are filled. Paragraphs are joined with '\n\n'. Width is measured in visible characters, so ANSI escapes are ignored (versionchanged 8.4.0).

tabs expanded to 8 columns
a '\b' paragraph keeps its internal newlines and relative indentation
empty text without preserve_paragraphs returns '' and drops initial_indent (see the test comment at tests/test_formatting.py:520-522)

interfaces.name: measure_table
interfaces.behavior: Takes an iterable of row tuples. Returns a tuple of the maximum term_len per column index, in column order.
edge_cases: empty rows give ()
rows of unequal length are handled per index

interfaces.name: iter_rows
interfaces.behavior: Yields each row right-padded with '' up to col_count columns.
edge_cases: rows already at col_count are unchanged
rows longer than col_count are not truncated

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter
interfaces.behavior: Buffering formatter. __init__(indent_increment=2, width=None, max_width=None). max_width defaults to 80. If width is None it uses module FORCED_WIDTH, else max(min(terminal columns, max_width) - 2, 50). Starts with current_indent=0 and an empty buffer list.
edge_cases: an explicit width bypasses the 50 minimum and FORCED_WIDTH
the shutil import is lazy

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write
interfaces.behavior: Appends a raw string to self.buffer with no processing.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indent
interfaces.behavior: Adds indent_increment to current_indent.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.dedent
interfaces.behavior: Subtracts indent_increment from current_indent. There is no floor at 0.
edge_cases: unbalanced dedent can make current_indent negative

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_usage
interfaces.behavior: Writes the usage line. The default prefix is gettext('Usage:') + ' '. The prefix is right-aligned in a field of current_indent characters, followed by 'prog '. If args is empty, only the prefix and prog are written with trailing spaces stripped, then '\n'. If text_width (width - current_indent) >= term_len(usage_prefix) + 20, args are wrapped to the right of the prefix with a hanging indent. Otherwise the prefix line is written alone and args go on following lines indented by max(current_indent, term_len(prefix)) + 4.
edge_cases: empty args gives 'Usage: Program\n'
a styled prefix is measured with term_len
an explicit prefix='' is honoured because the check is `is None`

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_heading
interfaces.behavior: Writes current_indent spaces, the heading, ':' and a newline.
edge_cases: the colon is always appended
the heading is not translated or wrapped

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_paragraph
interfaces.behavior: Writes '\n' only if the buffer is non-empty, so a blank line is never emitted first.
edge_cases: no-op on an empty buffer

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_text
interfaces.behavior: Wraps text at self.width with initial and subsequent indent equal to current_indent spaces, with preserve_paragraphs=True (so \b blocks work), then writes a trailing newline.
edge_cases: empty text writes '\n' only, or the indent plus newline depending on wrapper behaviour

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.write_dl
interfaces.behavior: Writes a definition list. col_max=30 and col_spacing=2 are the defaults. rows is materialised with list(). The first column width is min(max term_len, col_max) + col_spacing. If the term fits it is padded, otherwise the description starts on the next line at first_col + current_indent. The description is wrapped at max(width - first_col - 2, 10) with preserve_paragraphs=True. Continuation lines are indented by first_col + current_indent. A row with an empty second item writes only the term and a newline.
edge_cases: empty rows: widths is () so len != 2, which raises TypeError
a term wider than col_max pushes the description to the next line
an empty wrapped result writes '\n'
a row with an empty description is still counted as 2 columns

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.section
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that calls write_paragraph, then write_heading(name), then indent(). It dedents in a finally block.
edge_cases: dedent runs even if the body raises

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.indentation
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that indents and dedents in a finally block.

interfaces.name: HelpFormatter.getvalue
interfaces.behavior: Returns ''.join(self.buffer).
edge_cases: an empty buffer gives ''

interfaces.name: join_options
interfaces.behavior: Takes option strings and returns (', '.join(sorted opts), any_prefix_is_slash). Sorting is stable by the length of the prefix from parser._split_opt, so '-v' comes before '--verbose'. The flag is True if any prefix is '/'.
edge_cases: an empty iterable gives ('', False)
options with equal prefix length keep their input order

interfaces.name: FORCED_WIDTH

edge_cases: it only applies when width=None

gaps.description: dedent has no floor at zero and there is no guard against unbalanced indent and dedent calls.

gaps.description: There is no direct control over the wrapping of the description column, such as hanging indents or a configurable min text width. The minimum of 10 and the 2-column right margin are hard-coded.

gaps.description: There is no option to write to a stream, and no richer output such as a heading style. The formatter always buffers in memory and headings are plain text.

input.variation_strategy: Five features touch five different areas: post-parse option validation (core Option/Command), subcommand resolution (core Group), type conversion (types.Choice), interactive prompting (termui), and shell-completion post-processing (shell_completion). Each combines several interacting rules: sources and ordering, exact/alias/prefix precedence, exact-vs-prefix matching, attempt counting across failure kinds, and dedupe/sort/truncate ordering.

features.title: Option requires= and conflicts_with= constraints based on parameter source
features.problem: Click has no way to say that one option needs another or excludes another. Users hand-write checks in callbacks. A built-in constraint that understands where each value came from lets defaults and default_map values be ignored correctly.
public_interface: Option.__init__(..., requires: Sequence[str] | None = None, conflicts_with: Sequence[str] | None = None, ...)
Both hold parameter NAMES (e.g. 'beta'), not option strings; stored as tuples on Option.requires and Option.conflicts_with (empty tuple by default)
Command.parse_args runs the check after all handle_parse_result calls
behavior: An option is 'explicit' when ctx.get_parameter_source(name) is COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT or PROMPT (i.e. ParameterSource < DEFAULT_MAP). DEFAULT and DEFAULT_MAP are not explicit.

After all parameters are processed in Command.parse_args, params are visited in get_params order (declaration order). For each explicit Option that has constraints, first every name in conflicts_with is checked, then every name in requires, each in the listed order.
If a conflicts_with name is also explicit, raise UsageError (via ctx.fail) with message "Option '--alpha' cannot be used with '--beta'."
If a requires name is not explicit, raise UsageError with message "Option '--alpha' requires '--beta'."
The displayed option string is the longest string in the param's opts (first one on a tie). Exit code is 2 under CliRunner and the output contains 'Error: ' followed by the message.
The first violation found stops the check; only one error is reported.
interaction_rules: Conflicts are checked before requires on the same option, so an option that both conflicts with and requires 'b' reports the conflict when b is explicit.
A constraint declared on option A is only enforced when A is explicit; an explicit B that A requires does not impose anything on A.
A value that comes only from default or default_map never triggers a constraint and never satisfies a requires.
With ctx.resilient_parsing=True (e.g. shell completion) no constraint check runs.
edge_cases_and_errors: A name in requires/conflicts_with that matches no parameter of the command raises TypeError("Option 'alpha' refers to unknown parameter 'zzz'.") at parse time when the owning option is explicit (the first parameter name is the owning option's name).

Passing a plain str instead of a sequence raises TypeError("'requires' must be a sequence of parameter names, not a string.") from Option.__init__ (same wording with 'conflicts_with' for that argument).
An option that lists its own name raises ValueError("Option 'alpha' cannot refer to itself.") from Option.__init__.
A value supplied by envvar counts as explicit; a prompted value counts as explicit.
If the target is a flag given as --no-x it is explicit as well, as the source is COMMANDLINE.
backward_compatibility: Options without requires/conflicts_with behave exactly as before; Option.to_info_dict is unchanged.
The new keyword args default to None, so existing positional/keyword usage and subclasses keep working.

features.title: Group command aliases and unambiguous prefix matching
features.problem: Group.resolve_command only does exact lookup. Users want short aliases ('ci' for 'commit') and git-style abbreviations without writing custom Group subclasses.
public_interface: Group.__init__(..., allow_prefix_match: bool = False, **kwargs) stored as self.allow_prefix_match
Group.add_alias(self, alias: str, target: str) -> None
Group.resolve_command is extended (same signature)
behavior: Resolution order for args[0] (after make_str): 1) exact get_command match; 2) alias match; 3) the existing token_normalize_func retry (which then repeats steps 1 and 2 on the normalized token); 4) unique prefix match if allow_prefix_match.

An alias maps to a target command name via add_alias; resolution returns the CANONICAL target name as the first tuple element, so the sub-context info_name and invoked_subcommand are the canonical name.

Prefix matching considers names from list_commands(ctx) for which get_command(ctx, name) is not None and cmd.hidden is False, and that startwith the token. Exactly one match resolves to it (returning that canonical name). Aliases are not considered in prefix matching.
With several matches raise NoSuchCommand(token, message="Ambiguous command 'c'. Could be: commit, config.", ctx=ctx) listing matches sorted, joined by ', '.
With zero matches the existing NoSuchCommand with suggestions is raised.
An exact name or an alias always beats a prefix that would be ambiguous or would match something else.
interaction_rules: Exact command name beats an alias of the same spelling; add_alias for a spelling that already is a command name is allowed but never used.
An empty token never prefix-matches.
Prefix matching is skipped when ctx.resilient_parsing and the exact lookup failed only in the sense the existing code returns (None, None, rest); it must not raise when resilient.
Hidden commands are reachable by exact name or alias but never by prefix.

add_alias with an empty alias raises ValueError("Alias must not be empty.").
If an alias target is later removed from group.commands, resolution of the alias falls through to later steps as if the alias did not exist.
A token that looks like an option (starts with a prefix) keeps the existing parse_args behaviour when nothing matches; it is not prefix-matched.

That follows from the visiting rule, but it is not stated outright as a negative.

Validation in Option.__init__ for a str argument and for a self reference: the spec doesn't say which comes first if both happen at once (e.g. requires='alpha' on option 'alpha'). This case is not tested.

Behavior is undefined for an unknown target name when another violation that comes earlier in the order would also apply. The tests avoid that mix.

import pytest

import click
from click.exceptions import NoSuchCommand


def _make_group(**kwargs):
    @click.group(**kwargs)
    @click.pass_context
    def g(ctx):
        click.echo(f"invoked={ctx.invoked_subcommand}")

    @g.command()
    def status():
        ctx = click.get_current_context()
        click.echo(f"status info_name={ctx.info_name}")

    @g.command()
    def start():
        ctx = click.get_current_context()
        click.echo(f"start info_name={ctx.info_name}")

    return g


def _make_plain_group(**kwargs):
    g = click.Group("g", **kwargs)

    @g.command()
    def status():
        click.echo("s")

    @g.command()
    def start():
        click.echo("t")

    return g


# --- Criterion 1: alias resolves to canonical name ---------------------------


def test_alias_resolves_and_invoked_subcommand_is_canonical(runner):
    g = _make_group()
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["st"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "invoked=status\nstatus info_name=status\n"


def test_alias_example_output(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["st"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


def test_resolve_command_alias_returns_canonical_name():
    g = _make_plain_group()
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    ctx = click.Context(g)
    name, cmd, rest = g.resolve_command(ctx, ["st", "a", "b"])
    assert name == "status"
    assert cmd is g.commands["status"]
    assert rest == ["a", "b"]


def test_exact_name_beats_alias_of_same_spelling(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group()
    # Allowed, but never used because 'start' is a command name.
    g.add_alias("start", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["start"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "t\n"


def test_alias_beats_prefix_match(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    # 'stat' would prefix-match only 'status', but the alias wins.
    g.add_alias("stat", "start")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["stat"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "t\n"


def test_alias_beats_ambiguous_prefix(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    g.add_alias("sta", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sta"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


def test_alias_with_token_normalize_func(runner):
    g = _make_group(context_settings={"token_normalize_func": lambda x: x.lower()})
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["ST"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "invoked=status\nstatus info_name=status\n"


def test_alias_with_removed_target_falls_through_to_error(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group()
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    del g.commands["status"]
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["st"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'st'." in result.output


def test_alias_with_removed_target_falls_through_to_prefix(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    g.add_alias("st", "status")
    del g.commands["status"]
    # Alias is ignored; 'st' is now a unique prefix of 'start'.
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["st"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "t\n"


# --- Criterion 2: unique prefix resolves -------------------------------------


def test_unique_prefix_resolves(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["stat"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


def test_unique_prefix_invoked_subcommand_is_canonical(runner):
    g = _make_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    assert g.allow_prefix_match is True
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["star"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "invoked=start\nstart info_name=start\n"


def test_resolve_command_prefix_returns_canonical_name():
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    ctx = click.Context(g)
    name, cmd, rest = g.resolve_command(ctx, ["stat", "x"])
    assert name == "status"
    assert cmd is g.commands["status"]
    assert rest == ["x"]


def test_exact_name_beats_prefix(runner):
    g = click.Group("g", allow_prefix_match=True)

    @g.command("sta")
    def sta():
        click.echo("exact")

    @g.command()
    def status():
        click.echo("s")

    @g.command()
    def start():
        click.echo("t")

    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sta"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "exact\n"


def test_empty_token_never_prefix_matches(runner):
    g = click.Group("g", allow_prefix_match=True)

    @g.command()
    def status():
        click.echo("s")

    result = runner.invoke(g, [""])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "s\n" not in result.output
    assert "No such command ''." in result.output


def test_prefix_no_match_gives_no_such_command(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["xyz"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'xyz'." in result.output


def test_option_like_token_is_not_prefix_matched(runner):
    g = click.Group("g", allow_prefix_match=True)

    @g.command("-xyz")
    def weird():
        click.echo("weird")

    result = runner.invoke(g, ["--", "-x"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "weird" not in result.output
    assert "No such option" in result.output


def test_prefix_with_command_collection(runner):
    src = _make_plain_group()
    cc = click.CommandCollection("cc", sources=[src], allow_prefix_match=True)
    result = runner.invoke(cc, ["stat"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


def test_prefix_uses_overridden_hooks(runner):
    def lazy():
        click.echo("lazy")

    lazy_cmd = click.Command("lazyrun", callback=lazy)

    class LazyGroup(click.Group):
        def list_commands(self, ctx):
            return ["lazyrun", "ghost"]

        def get_command(self, ctx, cmd_name):
            if cmd_name == "lazyrun":
                return lazy_cmd
            # 'ghost' is listed but does not resolve.
            return None

    g = LazyGroup("g", allow_prefix_match=True)
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["la"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "lazy\n"

    result = runner.invoke(g, ["gh"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'gh'." in result.output


def test_alias_and_prefix_in_chain_mode(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(chain=True, allow_prefix_match=True)
    g.add_alias("s", "status")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["s", "star"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\nt\n"


# --- Criterion 3: ambiguous prefix -------------------------------------------


def test_ambiguous_prefix_exact_message(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sta"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "Ambiguous command 'sta'. Could be: start, status." in result.output


def test_ambiguous_prefix_raises_no_such_command():
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    ctx = click.Context(g)
    with pytest.raises(NoSuchCommand) as exc_info:
        g.resolve_command(ctx, ["sta"])
    assert exc_info.value.command_name == "sta"
    assert exc_info.value.ctx is ctx
    assert (
        exc_info.value.format_message()
        == "Ambiguous command 'sta'. Could be: start, status."
    )


def test_ambiguous_matches_are_sorted():
    class Unsorted(click.Group):
        def list_commands(self, ctx):
            return ["sc", "sa", "sb", "x"]

    g = Unsorted("g", allow_prefix_match=True)
    for name in ("sc", "sa", "sb", "x"):
        g.add_command(click.Command(name))

    ctx = click.Context(g)
    with pytest.raises(NoSuchCommand) as exc_info:
        g.resolve_command(ctx, ["s"])
    assert (
        exc_info.value.format_message()
        == "Ambiguous command 's'. Could be: sa, sb, sc."
    )


def test_resilient_parsing_suppresses_ambiguity_error():
    g = _make_plain_group(allow_prefix_match=True)
    ctx = click.Context(g, resilient_parsing=True)
    assert g.resolve_command(ctx, ["sta", "x"]) == (None, None, ["x"])


# --- Criterion 4: prefix matching off by default -----------------------------


def test_prefix_matching_off_by_default(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group()
    assert g.allow_prefix_match is False
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["stat"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'stat'." in result.output
    assert "Ambiguous" not in result.output


def test_prefix_matching_off_by_default_decorator(runner):
    g = _make_group()
    assert g.allow_prefix_match is False
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sta"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'sta'." in result.output
    assert "Ambiguous" not in result.output


def test_default_group_exact_resolution_unchanged(runner):
    g = _make_plain_group()
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["status"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


# --- Criterion 5: hidden commands --------------------------------------------


def _make_hidden_group():
    g = click.Group("g", allow_prefix_match=True)

    @g.command(hidden=True)
    def secret():
        click.echo("secret")

    return g


def test_hidden_command_not_prefix_matched(runner):
    g = _make_hidden_group()
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sec"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert "No such command 'sec'." in result.output
    assert "secret\n" not in result.output


def test_hidden_command_reachable_by_exact_name(runner):
    g = _make_hidden_group()
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["secret"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "secret\n"


def test_hidden_command_reachable_by_alias(runner):
    g = _make_hidden_group()
    g.add_alias("sx", "secret")
    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sx"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "secret\n"


def test_hidden_command_excluded_from_ambiguity(runner):
    g = click.Group("g", allow_prefix_match=True)

    @g.command()
    def status():
        click.echo("s")

    @g.command(hidden=True)
    def start():
        click.echo("t")

    result = runner.invoke(g, ["sta"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "s\n"


# --- Criterion 6: add_alias errors -------------------------------------------


def test_add_alias_unknown_target_raises_key_error():
    g = _make_plain_group()
    with pytest.raises(KeyError) as exc_info:
        g.add_alias("m", "missing")
    assert exc_info.value.args == ("missing",)


def test_add_alias_empty_alias_raises_value_error():
    g = _make_plain_group()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as exc_info:
        g.add_alias("", "status")
    assert str(exc_info.value) == "Alias must not be empty."


def test_add_alias_valid_returns_none():
    g = _make_plain_group()
    assert g.add_alias("st", "status") is None

import enum

import pytest

import click


class Fmt(enum.Enum):
    JSON = "j"
    JSONL = "jl"
    YAML = "y"


def _fmt_choice(**kwargs):
    return click.Choice(["json", "jsonl", "yaml"], **kwargs)


# --- 1. unique prefix returns original choice ---------------------------------


def test_prefix_match_attribute_stored():
    assert _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True).prefix_match is True
    assert _fmt_choice().prefix_match is False


def test_unique_prefix_returns_choice():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("y", None, None) == "yaml"
    assert c.convert("ya", None, None) == "yaml"
    assert c.convert("jsonl", None, None) == "jsonl"


def test_unique_prefix_longer_than_shared_part():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("jsonl", None, None) == "jsonl"


def test_unique_prefix_returns_original_enum_member():
    c = click.Choice(Fmt, prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("Y", None, None) is Fmt.YAML


def test_enum_prefix_compares_member_names_not_values():
    c = click.Choice(Fmt, prefix_match=True)
    # "y" is the value of YAML but not a prefix of any member name.
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter):
        c.convert("y", None, None)


def test_non_str_input_and_choices_return_original_object():
    c = click.Choice([10, 12, 20], prefix_match=True)
    result = c.convert(2, None, None)
    assert result == 20
    assert isinstance(result, int)


def test_prefix_respects_token_normalize_func():
    @click.command(context_settings={"token_normalize_func": str.lower})
    @click.option("--x", type=_fmt_choice(prefix_match=True))
    def cli(x):
        click.echo(repr(x))

    result = click.testing.CliRunner().invoke(cli, ["--x", "Y"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "'yaml'\n"


# --- 2. ambiguous prefix raises BadParameter with exact message ---------------


def test_ambiguous_prefix_message():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("js", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'js' is ambiguous: matches 'json', 'jsonl'."


def test_ambiguous_prefix_candidates_in_choice_order():
    c = click.Choice(["jsonl", "yaml", "json"], prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("j", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'j' is ambiguous: matches 'jsonl', 'json'."


def test_ambiguous_enum_lists_member_names():
    c = click.Choice(Fmt, prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("JS", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'JS' is ambiguous: matches 'JSON', 'JSONL'."


def test_duplicate_normalized_choices_are_ambiguous():
    c = click.Choice(["Json", "JSON"], case_sensitive=False, prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("js", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'js' is ambiguous: matches 'json', 'json'."


def test_ambiguous_non_str_input():
    c = click.Choice([10, 12, 20], prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert(1, None, None)
    assert "is ambiguous: matches '10', '12'." in exc_info.value.message


# --- 3. exact match wins over longer choices ----------------------------------


def test_exact_match_beats_prefix():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("json", None, None) == "json"


def test_exact_match_beats_prefix_case_insensitive():
    c = _fmt_choice(case_sensitive=False, prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("JSON", None, None) == "json"


def test_exact_enum_match_beats_prefix():
    c = click.Choice(Fmt, prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("JSON", None, None) is Fmt.JSON


# --- 4. case-insensitive prefix -----------------------------------------------


def test_case_insensitive_unique_prefix():
    c = click.Choice(["Json", "JSONL", "Yaml"], case_sensitive=False, prefix_match=True)
    assert c.convert("YA", None, None) == "Yaml"
    assert c.convert("y", None, None) == "Yaml"


def test_case_insensitive_ambiguous_uses_casefolded_candidates():
    c = click.Choice(["Json", "JSONL", "Yaml"], case_sensitive=False, prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("JS", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'JS' is ambiguous: matches 'json', 'jsonl'."


def test_case_sensitive_prefix_does_not_ignore_case():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("Y", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'Y' is not one of 'json', 'jsonl', 'yaml'."


# --- 5. empty string is invalid -----------------------------------------------


def test_empty_string_is_invalid_choice():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'' is not one of 'json', 'jsonl', 'yaml'."


def test_no_candidate_gives_invalid_choice_message():
    c = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("x", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == c.get_invalid_choice_message("x", ctx=None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'x' is not one of 'json', 'jsonl', 'yaml'."


# --- 6. default behaviour unchanged -------------------------------------------


def test_default_rejects_prefix():
    c = _fmt_choice()
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("y", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'y' is not one of 'json', 'jsonl', 'yaml'."


def test_default_rejects_ambiguous_prefix_with_invalid_message():
    c = _fmt_choice()
    with pytest.raises(click.BadParameter) as exc_info:
        c.convert("js", None, None)
    assert exc_info.value.message == "'js' is not one of 'json', 'jsonl', 'yaml'."


def test_default_exact_match_still_works():
    c = _fmt_choice()
    assert c.convert("yaml", None, None) == "yaml"
    assert click.Choice(Fmt).convert("YAML", None, None) is Fmt.YAML


def test_info_dict_has_no_new_key():
    for c in (_fmt_choice(), _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)):
        assert c.to_info_dict() == {
            "param_type": "Choice",
            "name": "choice",
            "choices": ("json", "jsonl", "yaml"),
            "case_sensitive": True,
        }


def test_missing_message_unchanged():
    a = _fmt_choice()
    b = _fmt_choice(prefix_match=True)
    assert b.get_missing_message(None, None) == a.get_missing_message(None, None)


# --- 7. end to end through CliRunner ------------------------------------------


def _make_cli():
    @click.command()
    @click.option("--x", type=_fmt_choice(prefix_match=True))
    def cli(x):
        click.echo(f"x={x}")

    return cli


def test_cli_unique_prefix(runner):
    result = runner.invoke(_make_cli(), ["--x", "y"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "x=yaml\n"


def test_cli_exact_match(runner):
    result = runner.invoke(_make_cli(), ["--x", "json"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert result.output == "x=json\n"


def test_cli_ambiguous_prefix(runner):
    result = runner.invoke(_make_cli(), ["--x", "js"])
    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert (
        "Invalid value for '--x': 'js' is ambiguous: matches 'json', 'jsonl'."
        in result.output
    )


def test_cli_ambiguous_attaches_ctx_and_param(runner):
    result = runner.invoke(_make_cli(), ["--x", "js"], standalone_mode=False)
    exc = result.exception
    assert isinstance(exc, click.BadParameter)
    assert exc.ctx is not None

def test_cli_empty_value_invalid(runner):

    assert result.exit_code == 2
    assert (

The spec says candidates are counted per original choice. But Choice._normalized_mapping (src/click/types.py:398-404) is a dict keyed by choice, and normalize_choice says each choice must have a unique normalized value (types.py:409). test_duplicate_normalized_choices_are_ambiguous uses two distinct originals ('Json', 'JSON') that casefold to the same string and expects "'js' is ambiguous: matches 'json', 'json'." The spec does not cover choices that are themselves equal duplicates.

The spec says 'with enum choices, prefixes compare against member names'. It does not say whether the case-sensitive default applies to member names. The tests assume it does: 'Y' matches YAML, and the lowercase 'y' (the member's value) is rejected.

The spec does not cover prefix matching with token_normalize_func directly; it only says normalize_choice is applied. test_prefix_respects_token_normalize_func assumes str.lower is applied to both the input and the choices before the prefix comparison.

import inspect

import pytest

import click


class Feeder:
    """Replacement for the termui prompt functions.

    Returns scripted answers in order and records every prompt text it was
    called with. Exceptions in the answer list are raised. When the answers
    run out, EOFError is raised (which click turns into Abort), so tests
    also check how many answers were consumed to distinguish an Abort caused
    by max_attempts from one caused by running out of input.
    """

    def __init__(self, answers):
        self.answers = list(answers)
        self.prompts = []

    def __call__(self, text):
        self.prompts.append(text)
        if not self.answers:
            raise EOFError()
        answer = self.answers.pop(0)
        if isinstance(answer, type) and issubclass(answer, BaseException):
            raise answer()
        return answer

    @property
    def reads(self):
        return len(self.prompts)


def feed(monkeypatch, answers):
    feeder = Feeder(answers)
    monkeypatch.setattr("click.termui.visible_prompt_func", feeder)
    monkeypatch.setattr("click.termui.hidden_prompt_func", feeder)
    return feeder


def error_lines(output):
    return [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.startswith("Error:")]


# 1. unlimited by default


def test_prompt_unlimited_by_default(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["bad"] * 10 + ["5"])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int) == 5
    assert feeder.reads == 11
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 10


def test_prompt_max_attempts_none_is_unlimited(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["bad"] * 10 + ["5"])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=None) == 5
    assert feeder.reads == 11
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 10


def test_confirm_unlimited_by_default(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x"] * 10 + ["y"])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=None) is True
    assert feeder.reads == 11
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert error_lines(out) == ["Error: invalid input"] * 10


def test_max_attempts_is_last_keyword_defaulting_to_none():
    for func in (click.prompt, click.confirm):
        params = list(inspect.signature(func).parameters.values())
        assert params[-1].name == "max_attempts"
        assert params[-1].default is None
    prompt_names = [p.name for p in inspect.signature(click.prompt).parameters.values()]
    assert prompt_names[:-1] == [
        "text",
        "default",
        "hide_input",
        "confirmation_prompt",
        "type",
        "value_proc",
        "prompt_suffix",
        "show_default",
        "err",
        "show_choices",
    ]
    confirm_names = [
        p.name for p in inspect.signature(click.confirm).parameters.values()
    ]
    assert confirm_names[:-1] == [
        "text",
        "default",
        "abort",
        "prompt_suffix",
        "show_default",
        "err",
    ]


# 2. prompt returns on the last allowed attempt


def test_prompt_returns_on_last_allowed_attempt(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "b", "5"])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=3) == 5
    assert feeder.reads == 3
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 2


def test_prompt_max_attempts_one_valid_first_answer(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["42"])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=1) == 42
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == []


def test_prompt_value_proc_usage_error_counts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    def proc(value):
        if value != "ok":
            raise click.UsageError("nope")
        return value

    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "ok"])
    assert click.prompt("v", value_proc=proc, max_attempts=2) == "ok"
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: nope"]


# 3. Abort raised exactly when failures reach max_attempts


def test_prompt_aborts_when_failures_reach_max(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "b", "5"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["5"]
    errors = error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)
    assert len(errors) == 2
    assert all(line.startswith("Error: ") for line in errors)


def test_prompt_max_attempts_one_bad_answer(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "5"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=1)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == [
        "Error: 'a' is not a valid integer."
    ]


def test_prompt_bool_max_attempts_true_means_one(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "5"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=True)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 1


def test_prompt_empty_answer_without_default_counts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["", "", "value"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("name", max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["value"]


def test_prompt_mixed_failure_kinds_share_one_count(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["", "a", "7"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["7"]


def test_prompt_hide_input_masked_error_on_final_failure(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["secret", "5"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("pin", type=int, hide_input=True, max_attempts=1)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "secret" not in out
    assert error_lines(out) == ["Error: '***' is not a valid integer."]


def test_prompt_keyboard_interrupt_aborts_immediately(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", KeyboardInterrupt, "5"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=5)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["5"]


def test_confirm_eof_aborts_immediately(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, [EOFError, "y"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=5)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert feeder.answers == ["y"]


# 4. confirm counts invalid input


def test_confirm_returns_after_one_invalid(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "y"])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=2) is True
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"]


def test_confirm_aborts_after_max_invalid(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "maybe", "y"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["y"]
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"] * 2


def test_confirm_max_attempts_one_bad_answer(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "y"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=1)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"]


def test_confirm_empty_with_default_none_counts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["", "", "n"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.confirm("ok?", default=None, max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["n"]


def test_confirm_valid_answers_on_last_attempt(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "z", "no"])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=3) is False
    assert feeder.reads == 3
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"] * 2


def test_confirm_abort_true_valid_no_still_aborts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["n", "y"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.confirm("ok?", abort=True, max_attempts=3)
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == []


def test_confirm_abort_true_valid_yes_after_invalid(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", "yes"])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", abort=True, max_attempts=2) is True
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"]


# 5. confirmation mismatch counts as one


def test_confirmation_mismatch_counts_once_and_restarts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "b", "c", "c"])
    assert click.prompt("p", confirmation_prompt=True, max_attempts=2) == "c"
    assert feeder.prompts == [
        "p: ",
        "Repeat for confirmation: ",
        "p: ",
        "Repeat for confirmation: ",
    ]
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == [
        "Error: The two entered values do not match."
    ]


def test_confirmation_mismatch_with_max_one_aborts(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", "b", "c", "c"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("p", confirmation_prompt=True, max_attempts=1)
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert feeder.answers == ["c", "c"]
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == [
        "Error: The two entered values do not match."
    ]


def test_confirmation_mismatch_and_conversion_error_share_count(
    monkeypatch, capsys
):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["1", "2", "q", "3", "3"])
    with pytest.raises(click.Abort):
        click.prompt("n", type=int, confirmation_prompt=True, max_attempts=2)
    assert feeder.reads == 3
    assert feeder.answers == ["3", "3"]
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 2


# 6. max_attempts=0 raises ValueError with exact message


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [0, -1, -5])
def test_prompt_invalid_max_attempts_raises_value_error(monkeypatch, value):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["5"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=value)
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "max_attempts must be at least 1."
    assert feeder.reads == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [0, -1, -5])
def test_confirm_invalid_max_attempts_raises_value_error(monkeypatch, value):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["y"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        click.confirm("ok?", max_attempts=value)
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "max_attempts must be at least 1."
    assert feeder.reads == 0


def test_bool_false_max_attempts_raises_value_error(monkeypatch):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["5"])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        click.prompt("n", type=int, max_attempts=False)
    assert str(excinfo.value) == "max_attempts must be at least 1."
    assert feeder.reads == 0


# 7. default-accepted empty answer does not count


def test_prompt_default_accepted_with_max_one(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, [""])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int, default=7, max_attempts=1) == 7
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == []


def test_prompt_default_accepted_after_failure(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["a", ""])
    assert click.prompt("n", type=int, default=3, max_attempts=2) == 3
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert len(error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out)) == 1


def test_confirm_default_accepted_with_max_one(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, [""])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", default=True, max_attempts=1) is True
    assert feeder.reads == 1
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == []


def test_confirm_default_accepted_after_failure(monkeypatch, capsys):
    feeder = feed(monkeypatch, ["x", ""])
    assert click.confirm("ok?", default=False, max_attempts=2) is False
    assert feeder.reads == 2
    assert error_lines(capsys.readouterr().out) == ["Error: invalid input"]

ambiguities: An empty answer with default=None counts as a failed attempt, but the current code (src/click/termui.py:261-270 for prompt, 337-341 for confirm) prints no error line for an empty prompt() answer. The spec doesn't say whether the gold version adds one. So the empty-answer prompt tests only check how many answers were read and that Abort is raised, not the output.

The spec says the masked error line is printed when hide_input is set. The tests expect the existing masking format "Error: '***' is not a valid integer.", taken from _HIDDEN_INPUT_MASK (termui.py:58), _mask_hidden_input (termui.py:71) and the IntParamType message (types.py:605). That assumes the error text itself does not change.
When a default value fails conversion via value_proc (e.g. an out-of-range default), the spec doesn't say whether that counts as a failed attempt. No test depends on it.

The spec does not say whether ValueError for max_attempts < 1 is raised before or after validating other arguments. The tests only check it happens before any input is read. Reading False as 0, and therefore a ValueError, comes from the rule that bools follow int semantics.
notes: How the tests run: they monkeypatch click.termui.visible_prompt_func and hidden_prompt_func (the hook used at termui.py:236 and 330, and also in tests/test_utils/test_prompt.py:81-82) with a scripted feeder. When the scripted answers run out the feeder raises EOFError, which becomes Abort. So every Abort test also checks how many answers were read and which were left over, to tell a max_attempts Abort apart from running out of input.
The error output is read with capsys. Because the prompt function is mocked, the prompt text itself is never echoed, so only the 'Error:' lines show up in stdout.

No test for 'Option.prompt_for_value unchanged' was written: it would pass on the base code too, so it can't be a FAIL_TO_PASS test. It is better covered by the existing regression tests (tests/test_options.py, tests/test_termui.py).
test_max_attempts_is_last_keyword_defaulting_to_none checks the positional parameter order using inspect.signature. The spec says the new keyword is appended last and the existing order is kept.

Regression test files to consider for PASS_TO_PASS: tests/test_utils/test_prompt.py and tests/test_termui.py, plus the confirm/prompt-related tests in tests/test_options.py. Final IDs have not been selected yet.
